A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP geometry, conformity, and vSLERP research. Text, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including v2's integrated appendices and its partly duplicative appended supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP embedding statistics, loss-shifting experiments, Gaussian simulations, conformity analyses, generator comparisons, and vSLERP examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a norm-distribution analysis with examples of high-norm captions.

M1.justification: The conformity estimator, contrastive-loss formulation, embedding shifts, and vSLERP procedure remain unchanged. Renaming raw embeddings as primary embeddings and adding a norm diagnostic do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MS-COCO, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, synthetic Gaussian examples, and the same generation and interpolation tasks. The new caption-norm analysis uses already covered MS-COCO data.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain unCLIP and Glide for image generation, ClipCap and Caption Reward for captioning, and SLERP versus vSLERP for interpolation. No comparator is added or removed from these comparisons.

E3.justification: Figure 14 adds a diagnostic examining unnormalized caption norms and examples from their upper tail. Existing protocols retain the 5,000-sample single-batch loss evaluation, alpha sweep from -1 to 1, CLIP backbones, and 1,000-vector Gaussian simulation.

E4.justification: v2 adds a case analysis connecting large embedding norms with unusual captions, shown in Figure 14 and repeated as supplementary Figure 2. The whitening analysis, larger-backbone checks, alternative ellipsoid shifts, out-of-distribution examples, and vSLERP case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing distribution statistics and correlation reporting remain unchanged; the new histogram does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports the caption-norm histogram and high-norm caption examples. Matched existing findings remain unchanged, including 100% two-feature modality separation, Pearson correlation 0.9998, conformity-distribution KL divergence approximately 0.14 at alpha = 0, and the generator comparisons in Figure 13.

T1.justification: The thin-shell theorem, mathematical definitions, geometric properties, and derivations are retained. Although whitening theory is missing from v2's integrated Appendix B, its definition, claim, and derivations remain in the appended supplement, Section 2.1, on PDF pages 21–22.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds the explicit claim that embedding magnitude carries meaningful semantic information despite cosine normalization. The central double-ellipsoid, conformity, modality-gap, and vSLERP contributions retain their original scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets unusually large caption norms as semantically meaningful and uses this observation to motivate studying pre-normalized embeddings. Existing explanations involving false negatives, semantic blurring, conformity matching, and the limitations of a Gaussian embedding approximation remain.

D1.justification: v1 Section 7.2 recommends -2 <= alpha <= 2 for visually appealing vSLERP outputs; v2 omits this practical parameter guidance. This is a loss of documentation, without evidence that the underlying generation settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes its origin-directed shifts from Liang et al.'s embedding-shift experiment and connects semantic blurring to Schrodi et al.'s entropy discussion. It removes references to Eldar and Oppenheim, Kessy et al., and Huynh et al.; most research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around three motivations, and the semantic-blur discussion, applications, conclusion, and numerous captions are condensed or rewritten. Supplementary material is reorganized into Appendices A–C and then largely repeated in a separate supplement. Terminology and citation style also change throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICML layout, relocates and resizes numerous figures, adds the norm-distribution figure, and repeats most appendix figures under separate numbering. Figure 13 reverses its two panels without updating the caption's top/bottom descriptions. The appended supplement includes anonymous-author placeholders, review line numbers, and an AUTHORERR message.

improvement.justification: The new norm/caption diagnostic and clearer positioning provide limited benefits. However, v2 introduces a confusing duplicated supplement with unfinished author metadata, an incorrect panel-order description in Figure 13, and removes useful vSLERP parameter guidance. With the central scientific evidence otherwise unchanged, these defects produce a modest net decline in clarity and reproducibility.
